title: The creed said together
hookLine: a whole congregation saying what they believe in one voice

cards: The sermon ends. The whole room stands, with a creak of benches and a shuffle of coats, and the minister begins: "I believe in one God." By the third word, everyone has caught up.
Some read from a card. Some have known it since they were small. An old man says every word like he's signing his name.
Near the back, a woman pauses at a line she's wrestling with, then picks it up at the next one. One long paragraph, said by a whole room in one voice. Today: the creed said together.

teach.b: Day two hundred ninety-seven gave the creed its name, from credo, I believe. A creed is a short summary of the faith, said out loud, and Christians trace the habit back to the New Testament.
Start with Paul, writing to Corinth.

He hands on something he says was handed to him: "For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures."
Received, then delivered, like a family recipe nobody wrote alone. Next, the mouth.

teach.h: WITH THE MOUTH, NOT ONLY THE HEART.
teach.b: In Romans, Paul puts belief and speech side by side: "For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation." Faith isn't only kept inside. It gets said.
Then, the room. In some churches the Nicene Creed or the Apostles' Creed is said every Sunday.

The old English prayer book has it begin, "I believe." Other churches say, "We believe." Some Christians describe that as leaning on the church on a day when their own faith feels thin: nobody carries every word alone.
Not every church recites a creed. Quakers and some Baptist churches, for reasons of conscience, prefer not to make any set words a test. Last, a father in Mark's Gospel.
Jesus tells him all things are possible to the one who believes, and the father cries out: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief." Both halves, in one breath.

how: In Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican, Lutheran and some other churches, the congregation says or sings the Nicene Creed or the Apostles' Creed together during the service; Quakers and some Baptist churches do not recite a creed in worship.

games.q: what does “the creed said together” mean?
o: a summary of faith a whole church says aloud at once
a private vow each believer writes for themselves
a hymn the choir sings while the people sit

p: with the mouth confession is made
two ways the creed can begin

s: a creed is meant to be kept silently, in the heart
Romans puts heart and mouth together: "with the mouth confession is made." in church it's said aloud, together.
Quakers say the creed together at their meetings
Quakers and some Baptist churches don't make any set words a test, for reasons of conscience.
Paul says he received what he handed on
"I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received." a creed is passed hand to hand.

games.q: you're the father in Mark's Gospel. your son is suffering, and Jesus tells you all things are possible to the one who believes. what do you say?
o: "I believe, and I have no doubt at all."
"Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief."
"I'll believe it when I see it."
games.why: he says both at once: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief." belief and struggle in a single breath.

practice: If you know a creed, say its opening line out loud, slowly, even alone, and notice what changes when the words leave your mouth; if you don't, read the line on the screen.
If you pray, you can add the father's words from Mark: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief. If belief isn't where you are today, simply listen, and notice which word stays with you.

wordCard.voice: The creed said together. A short summary of the faith, handed on and spoken aloud by a whole room at once.

orig.note: Greek: I believe, the verb Mark's father uses when he cries out to Jesus.

carryVoice: Your line: we believe. A whole room, one voice, nobody carrying it alone. See you tomorrow.
